sections.h2: How did the Town of Palm Tree come to exist?
sections.html:
Palm Tree became an Orange County town on January 1, 2019, and its borders match the village of Kiryas Joel exactly. Voters approved the split from the Town of Monroe in a referendum on November 7, 2017, and a 2018 state law moved the start date up by a year. In 2019 residents also chose a single consolidated town and village government that operates like a village (Wikipedia).

The land totals 1.5 square miles, nearly all of it dry apart from a small pond near the center, which works out to roughly 22,540 people per square mile. The 2020 census counted 32,954 residents, and the Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 47,147, up 43.1 percent from its 2020 base.

Older deeds, tax maps and surveys may describe the parcel as part of Monroe or of the village, while current records use Palm Tree. Make sure your deed, tax bill and survey all describe the same lot before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What does the Census show about housing in Palm Tree?
sections.html:
Households here are large, and a third of occupied homes are owned by their residents. QuickFacts shows 7,505 households averaging 5.08 people, an owner share of 33.4 percent, a typical owned home valued at $758,800 and median rent of $1,604 (Census Bureau).

  • Owner monthly cost: $2,616 with a mortgage and $1,075 without
  • Population under 18: 55.2 percent, including 18.4 percent under 5
  • Population 65 and older: 2.4 percent
  • Middle household income: $50,032 in 2024 dollars
  • Commute: 18.9 minutes on average
  • Residents who had not moved in the past year: 95.3 percent

A buyer's appraiser will look at how each unit in a house is used, so gather floor plans, unit counts and rent figures before you ask for offers.

sections.h2: Which office records a deed for a Palm Tree property?
sections.html:
Deeds go to the Orange County Clerk in Goshen. The Record Room is on the second floor of the Government Center at 255 Main Street, and the clerk keeps deeds, mortgages, satisfactions, federal tax liens, judgments and lis pendens (Record Room).

  • Public computers in the office are free for searching records, and an online search site exists too.
  • Plain copies cost $0.65 a page with a $1.30 minimum; certified copies cost $1.25 a page with a $5.00 minimum.
  • The clerk says a copy of your own deed runs about $5 and warns about companies that charge to fetch one.
  • A free Fraud Alert service notifies owners when a deed or mortgage is recorded under their name (County Clerk).

Search for judgments and liens against your name before you list. A seller who finds one early can arrange the payoff, and the title search will turn it up anyway.

sections.h2: When are Palm Tree property taxes collected, and how are they challenged?
sections.html:
Orange County gives a general pattern, and the local tax collector gives the exact dates. The county's assessors page lists the periods below and tells owners to call their municipality's tax collector for a precise schedule (Orange County).

Type of tax billUsual collection period in Orange County
County and townJanuary through March
SchoolSeptember through November
VillageJune through October

Source: Orange County Assessors page.

Because Palm Tree and Kiryas Joel are the same territory, ask the tax collector which of these bills apply to your parcel. Questions about delinquent amounts and penalties go to the county finance office at 845-291-2480.

On assessments, the state tax department says Grievance Day is the fourth Tuesday of May in most communities and tells owners to confirm the date with the local assessor (tax.ny.gov). Form RP-524 goes to the assessor or the board of assessment review, filing costs nothing, and only the current tentative roll can be challenged. Palm Tree's date for next year is a question for its assessor.

sections.h2: What state transfer tax and forms apply to a Palm Tree sale?
sections.html:
Albany charges two dollars on each $500 of price, counting a partial $500 as whole, and the seller pays unless the contract says otherwise (tax.ny.gov). A sale at Palm Tree's typical owned-home value of $758,800 rounds to $759,000, which is 1,518 slices and $3,036.

The combined return, Form TP-584, goes to the county clerk, and the form and tax are due within 15 days after the deed is delivered. A residence priced at $1 million or more also carries a 1 percent mansion tax, paid by the buyer.

One rule matters to investors. When a limited liability company buys or sells a building with up to four dwelling units, the state will not accept the return unless it comes with names and addresses for every member, manager and other authorized person. If a member is itself a company, the list continues until natural persons are identified. Collect that information before the closing date.

sections.h2: What must a Palm Tree seller disclose when tenants live in the house?
sections.html:
The owner of a house with up to four units signs the state's seller form and gives it to the buyer ahead of the contract signature (Real Property Law 462). The statute leaves room for as-is sales, and the form is not a warranty.

Question 4 asks whether anyone besides the owner holds a lease, easement or other right to use or occupy part of the property. With an owner share of 33.4 percent, many Palm Tree buyers will ask about leases and rents right away, so collect copies and a rent roll before you list. The form also covers certificates of occupancy, shared walls or driveways, flood zones, water and sewage service, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors and the condition of the roof, heating and plumbing.

Because the town and village governments were combined, ask Palm Tree town hall which office issues building permits and certificates of occupancy for your address. Get the answer in writing if past work was done on the house.

sections.h2: When does a cash offer suit a Palm Tree property?
sections.html: It can suit an owner who wants a short timeline, a house with deferred repairs or a building with occupied units. With no lender in the picture, the closing depends on payoffs, a clear title search and recording in Goshen. Get the offer in writing, confirm who pays each transfer cost, and have a New York attorney read the contract before signing.

faqs.q: Is Palm Tree simply another name for Kiryas Joel?
faqs.a: The boundaries are identical. The town was created on January 1, 2019 and is coterminous with the village of Kiryas Joel, which had been part of the Town of Monroe. A deed may name either one, so check which description your title company uses.

faqs.q: Where does a Palm Tree deed get recorded?
faqs.a: At the Orange County Clerk in Goshen, in the Record Room on the second floor of the Government Center, 255 Main Street. The office also runs a free Fraud Alert that tells owners when a deed or mortgage is recorded in their name.

faqs.q: What would the state transfer tax be on a $759,000 Palm Tree sale?
faqs.a: $3,036, at two dollars per $500. The seller normally pays it, and the buyer pays the 1 percent mansion tax only when a residence reaches $1 million. Form TP-584 and the payment go to the county clerk within 15 days of the deed's delivery.

faqs.q: In which months does Orange County collect county and town tax?
faqs.a: Generally January through March, while school bills are collected September through November. The county says periods vary by municipality, so the Palm Tree tax collector has the final schedule for your bill.

faqs.q: Must a Palm Tree seller mention tenants to a buyer?
faqs.a: Yes. The state form asks whether anyone other than the owner has a lease or a right to use or occupy any part of the property. Answer from your own knowledge, attach extra pages if needed, and hand the form over before the contract is signed.
